chunks: First-order LPF and HPF circuits. The question: Draw a circuit for a first-order LPF/HPF.
A first-order filter is one resistor and one capacitor (or, less often, an inductor, which is a coil) that lets some frequencies through and blocks others.
A low-pass filter passes slow signals and cuts fast ones. A high-pass filter does the opposite.
The only difference between them is which part sits in series and which goes to ground.
For the low-pass, picture a bucket fed through a narrow pipe. Slow changes in the water supply fill and empty the bucket, so the level follows them.
Fast flutters are too quick for the narrow pipe, so they get averaged out. For the high-pass, picture a rubber membrane across a pipe.
A steady push stretches it and then nothing more flows, but a quick back-and-forth push passes right through.
Same two parts, swapped. In the low-pass, the capacitor to ground diverts high frequencies.
In the high-pass, the series capacitor blocks low frequencies and the resistor to ground sets the DC level. Both have f c equals 1 over (2 pi times 10 kilohms times 15.
9 nanofarads ) about 1 kilohertz.
Capacitor: stores charge. It blocks steady (DC) current but lets changing signals pass. Corner frequency: where the output has dropped to 70. 7% of its passband value.
For RC it is 1 over (2 pi RC) . Series / to ground: in series sits in the signal path. To ground connects the output node to 0 volts.
Loading: whatever you connect to the output draws current and shifts the filter's behavior. Buffer: an amplifier stage that copies a voltage without drawing current from it.
Use R equals 1. 6 kilohms and C equals 100 nanofarads. The corner is 1 over (2 pi times 1600 times 10 to the -7) , about 1 kilohertz.
Put R in series and C to ground, take the output across C, and you have a low-pass. Swap their places and you have a high-pass with the same corner. That is the whole idea.
"The RC low-pass is a series resistor with a capacitor to ground, output across the capacitor. The capacitor shorts out high frequencies.
The high-pass swaps them: series capacitor, resistor to ground, output across the resistor, so the capacitor blocks DC. Both have a corner at 1 over (2 pi RC) .
You can build the same filters with an inductor, series L plus a resistor to ground for a low-pass, but RC is usually preferred.
And note that loading shifts the corner, so buffer it or use an active stage if needed."
